title: Analogies
lines: USAT's Verbal Reasoning section usually opens with about five analogy questions. Each gives a pair of words in capitals, such as DOCTOR : HOSPITAL, and four pairs as options. You must pick the pair whose words are linked in the same way as the stem pair. The test is not about hard vocabulary; it is about naming relationships precisely.
## The method in four steps
- Read the stem pair and make a sentence that links the two words: "A doctor works in a hospital."
- Make the sentence specific. "A doctor is found in a hospital" is too loose; "A doctor works in a hospital" is better.
- Put each option pair into the same sentence, keeping the order: "A teacher works in a school" fits; "A school works in a teacher" does not.
- If two options fit, tighten the sentence and test again. Only one option should survive.
! Keep the order. If the stem is PART : WHOLE, an option written WHOLE : PART is wrong even though the link looks similar.
## The common relationship types
| Type | Stem example | Matching pair
| Synonyms | BRAVE : COURAGEOUS | happy : joyful
| Antonyms | ANCIENT : MODERN | generous : stingy
| Part and whole | PAGE : BOOK | brick : wall
| Member and class | SPARROW : BIRD | cobra : snake
| Worker and workplace | PILOT : COCKPIT | chef : kitchen
| Worker and tool | TAILOR : NEEDLE | carpenter : saw
| Worker and product | POET : POEM | baker : bread
| Tool and action | KNIFE : CUT | broom : sweep
| Cause and effect | FIRE : SMOKE | virus : illness
| Degree (intensity) | WARM : HOT | drizzle : downpour
| Object and material | SHIRT : COTTON | ring : gold
| Young and adult | CALF : COW | cub : lion
| Animal and home | BEE : HIVE | horse : stable
| Organ and function | EAR : HEAR | lung : breathe
| Unit and quantity | METRE : LENGTH | litre : volume
| Symbol or sign | DOVE : PEACE | crescent : Islam
| Lack of | DROUGHT : RAIN | darkness : light
## Worked examples
> PUPPY : DOG
> (A) kitten : mouse  (B) foal : horse  (C) nest : bird  (D) lamb : wool
> Sentence: "A puppy is a young dog." A foal is a young horse, so B fits. A kitten is not a young mouse, a nest is a bird's home, and lamb : wool is animal and product.
> DRIZZLE : DOWNPOUR
> (A) whisper : shout  (B) rain : cloud  (C) wind : storm  (D) river : sea

> Sentence: "A drizzle is a much weaker form of a downpour." A whisper is a much weaker form of a shout: A. Wind : storm is tempting, but a storm is not simply stronger wind; it includes rain and lightning. River : sea is a flow into a larger body, not degree.
> SURGEON : SCALPEL
> (A) farmer : wheat  (B) painter : brush  (C) judge : court  (D) author : book
> Sentence: "A surgeon works with a scalpel as a tool." A painter works with a brush: B. Wheat is the farmer's product, court the judge's workplace, and book the author's product.
## How to break a tie

When two options seem to fit, ask a sharper question. For PEN : WRITE, both "axe : chop" and "chair : sit" fit a loose sentence ("used to"). Sharpen it: a pen is a tool used to perform an action on something. An axe chops wood; a chair is not used to act on anything. Choose axe : chop.
Also check the category of each word. If the stem is NOUN : VERB, the answer is usually NOUN : VERB too. If the stem is a person and a place, look for a person and a place.
## Traps to avoid

! Same topic is not same relationship. For DOCTOR : PATIENT, the option nurse : hospital shares the medical topic but shows worker and workplace, not professional and person served. Teacher : student is the right kind of match.
! Do not choose a pair because the words look alike or rhyme. Always test the sentence.
! Degree pairs must move the same way. If the stem goes from mild to strong (ANNOYED : FURIOUS), an option that goes from strong to mild (ecstatic : pleased) is reversed.
! Do not bring in a personal association. ROSE : RED is not a firm rule (roses come in many colours); the test prefers relationships that are always true.
## Quick check
- Make a precise sentence for the stem, then test every option in order.
- Learn the main relationship types and say the type in your head.
- Watch the direction of the pair and the parts of speech.
- If two fit, tighten the sentence; never guess on topic alone.
